<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, as in #60397. No other open PR ports these kernels to gfx942.

The PR is stacked on #60397 and merges its head 9a24c32a17. Its own commits are the 8 after 73f40ed and the 7 after that merge. Until #60397 merges, the diff against `main` includes #60397.

**Speculative decoding works at every concurrency.** The mono path takes decode steps of up to 42 rows on gfx942, which is up to 7 concurrent requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A step of 8 or more requests runs vLLM's path, with the same speculative decoding, and gets none of the speedup. That limit needs to be fixed, and we are working on it (see Follow-ups).

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, 5 DSpark drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points, because there is no `main` run at these concurrencies: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×). Total throughput per GPU goes from 4,255 to 6,729 tokens/s (1.58×), from 6,315 to 8,882 (1.41×) and from 10,998 to 14,839 (1.35×).
- A standard decoder layer runs as 2 kernels instead of 32, in 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` averages 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 (pooled p 0.49). Over all 5 runs of `main` and the 9 runs of this PR's versions, the mono path is 0.14 points lower (p 0.54). Neither difference is significant. The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, where vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.
- gfx950 is unchanged. A compile-only gfx950 build of the 20 kernels before and after this PR gives the same instruction counts, apart from 1 or 2 `s_waitcnt` and `s_nop`. No MI355X was used.
- The gfx942 kernels run only with the switch on, on gfx942. Two small changes apply without the switch, see "Changes outside the switch".

## Requirements of the gfx942 mono path

Mono kernels are built for fixed shapes. A deployment or a step outside these limits runs vLLM's own path.

| | gfx942 (this PR) | gfx950 (#60397) |
|---|---|---|
| Tensor parallel size | 4 | 2 or 4 |
| Rows a decode step, requests × (1 + drafts) | at most 42 | at most 48 |
| Concurrency with 5 DSpark drafts | up to 7 | up to 8 |
| Concurrency without drafts | up to 40 with FULL CUDA graphs, 42 in eager mode | up to 48 |
| Steps | decode only, eager or a FULL CUDA graph | same |
| KV cache | `fp8_ds_mla` | same |
| MoE | DeepSeek-V4.1 routing: 384 experts, top 6, sqrtsoftplus, ×1.5, a shared expert. The draft layers use 128 experts and top 3. | same, no draft layers |

- The row limit comes from LDS. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950. So a gfx942 GEMV pass holds the x rows of 6 tokens instead of 16, and a step of 12 to 42 rows runs 2 to 7 passes on weights loaded once.
- A FULL CUDA graph step runs padded to the next graph size, and the mono path takes the padded step. With 5 DSpark drafts the graph sizes are 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 42 and 48 rows, so a step of 5 requests runs as 36 rows.
- At TP2 on gfx942 the path logs one line, and every layer runs vLLM's path. A TP size other than 2 or 4 is an error at startup, as in #60397.
- A step outside the limits, for example prefill, a mixed step, more than 42 rows or a PIECEWISE graph, runs vLLM's path on every layer and every rank. Both paths take and return the same tensors at each layer, so the engine can switch between them from one step to the next.

## Validation

**Setup.** MI325X, TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`. Both arms use one image, one command and one environment, listed under Reproduce. They differ only in the `vllm` package and in `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE`.

- `main`: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` as it is (vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev88+g81198e97b, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1, amd-aiter 0.1.24.post1).
- PR: the same image, with the `vllm/` changes of #60397 and this PR copied over its `vllm` package (see Reproduce). The changes that came into this branch with `main` and #60397 after 242e4213 are not in the PR arm.

### AgentX, concurrency 1, against `main`

One 3,600 s run per arm, each on a fresh server, with the InferenceX AgentX client. Interactivity is 1 / the inter-token latency, so P90 is the slow tail. Throughput is the input and output tokens of the measured requests over the run time, divided by the 4 GPUs.

| | `main` | PR | PR / `main` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured requests, no errors | 239 | 306 | |
| Interactivity P50 (tokens/s/user) | 216.85 | 503.53 | 2.32× |
| Interactivity P90 (tokens/s/user) | 182.25 | 411.26 | 2.26× |
| Interactivity mean (tokens/s/user) | 200.43 | 461.94 | 2.30× |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 0.510 | 0.544 | |
| Total throughput per GPU (tokens/s) | 4,024 | 6,546 | 1.63× |

- Concurrency 1 is one recorded Claude Code session at a time, not one request at a time. When the recorded agent ran subagents in parallel, the replay sends their requests at the same time. 34 of the PR's 305 requests overlap another request, in steps of 12 or 18 rows, and take the mono path too. Their median interactivity is 392, against 178 on `main`.
- All 239 requests of the `main` run are also in the PR run, with the same output lengths. On those, the PR's inter-token latency is 0.429× `main`'s at the median (P10 0.420, P90 0.450).
- The PR run is from an earlier version of 2dd3ff8 that took steps of up to 30 rows. Its decode TPOT at steps of 6, 12 and 18 rows is 1.86, 2.46 and 3.21 ms, against 1.86, 2.38 and 3.10 ms on 2dd3ff8.

### AgentX, concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points

There is no `main` run at these concurrencies. The published points are InferenceX's MI325X AgentX results at TP4 from [Actions run 35637516947](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35637516947), with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984` and InferenceX's own recipe. That is an older nightly, so it stands in for `main` only roughly. At concurrency 1 the published point is close to our `main` run: P90 189.90 against 182.25, and 3,913 against 4,024 tokens/s per GPU.

Interactivity is in tokens/s/user, TTFT in seconds and throughput in tokens/s per GPU. The ratios are against the published point at the same concurrency.

| Concurrency | Run | Measured requests, no errors | Interactivity P50 | Interactivity P90 | Interactivity mean | TTFT P50 | Total throughput per GPU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | Published | 378 | 215.71 | 153.22 | 170.09 | 0.653 | 4,255 |
| 2 | PR, 2dd3ff8 | 493 | 501.98 (2.33×) | 368.64 (2.41×) | 400.82 (2.36×) | 0.417 | 6,729 (1.58×) |
| 4 | Published | 539 | 196.51 | 142.75 | 159.96 | 0.537 | 6,315 |
| 4 | PR, 06007b2 | 673 | 491.35 (2.50×) | 316.28 (2.22×) | 379.47 (2.37×) | 0.369 | 8,882 (1.41×) |
| 8 | Published | 1,112 | 146.76 | 81.52 | 120.31 | 0.514 | 10,998 |
| 8 | PR, 06007b2 | 1,373 | 317.99 (2.17×) | 162.61 (1.99×) | 258.60 (2.15×) | 0.397 | 14,839 (1.35×) |

- At concurrency 2 at most 3 requests decoded at once, and at concurrency 4 at most 5. So every decode step had at most 30 rows, 36 with the graph padding, and took the mono path.
- At concurrency 8 at most 8 requests decoded at once. Steps of more than 42 rows run vLLM's path, and they took 0.14% of the time with any request decoding. 1 request decoded during 45.6% of that time, 2 during 27.2%, 3 during 15.4% and 4 or more during 11.8%.
- Requests that decoded alone have an interactivity P50 of 509, 508 and 511 at concurrency 2, 4 and 8. Requests that overlapped another request have a median of 390, 386 and 299.

### What runs on each layer

Torch profiler on rank 0, 40 engine steps under AgentX traffic, each step 1 request with 6 rows. The numbers are medians over 39 decode periods on `main` and 35 on the PR. A period runs from the start of one decode step to the start of the next, so it includes the lm_head, sampling and the DSpark drafter. The profile is of the first version of this PR (983ec3b), which took steps of 6 rows only.

| | `main` | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode period (ms) | 17.92 | 7.20 |
| Target forward (ms) | 15.85 | 5.98 |
| Kernels in a period | 1,901 | 340 |
| Kernels in layers 0 to 39 | 1,581 | 180 |
| GPU time after the forward: lm_head, sampling, DSpark drafter (ms) | 2.03 | 1.18 |

<details>
<summary>Each layer type, a standard layer part by part, and the timelines</summary>

| Layers | Layer type | Kernels a layer, `main` | Kernels a layer, PR | GPU time a layer, `main` (µs) | GPU time a layer, PR (µs) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | window only, first layer | 172 | 9 | 941 | 172 |
| 1 | window only, Engram | 40 | 9 | 417 | 205 |
| 2, 8 | index | 48 | 14 | 485 | 236 |
| 14 | index, Engram | 55 | 21 | 557 | 318 |
| 20 | index, writes the candidate blocks | 64 | 15 | 621 | 322 |
| 24, 28, 32, 36 | index, candidate logits | 47 | 8 | 532 | 167 |
| the 27 standard layers from 3 to 36 | standard | 32 | 2 | 320 | 115 |
| 37, 38, 39 | standard, hidden states kept for DSpark | 34 | 4 | 335 | 133 |

- On `main`, 141 of layer 0's 172 kernels are small elementwise and reduce kernels. The folded form of the first layer's entry seam has no AITER kernel on gfx942, so it runs the eager reference. With this PR, layer 0 runs as a whole mono layer and takes the unfolded form, which AITER's fused seam kernel covers.
- What still runs outside the mono launches with this PR: the Engram lookup and projection (layers 0, 1 and 14), vLLM's compressor and indexer on the index layers with the gfx942 top-512 and key list, and vLLM's mHC post and mean before layers 37 to 39, which make the hidden states the drafter reads.
- After the forward, the 5 Markov steps of the drafter take 1 launch each (5 × about 18 µs) instead of about 9 kernels each, and the 3 draft layers end in `dsv41_mono_ffn` (about 50 µs each).

A standard layer, one of the 30 (3 to 7, 9 to 13, 15 to 19, 21 to 23, 25 to 27, 29 to 31, 33 to 35, 37 to 39). The `main` column is layer 5 of one period.

### Accuracy

**GSM8K.** `lm_eval` `gsm8k` (the stock task), 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, greedy, at most 512 new tokens, through `/v1/completions`. Both arms use DSpark block rejection for these runs, so the target model checks every draft token. At concurrency 7 the steps have 6 to 42 rows, and with this PR all of them take the mono path. Strict-match of each run:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1 | 0.9340, 0.9318 | 0.9272 (827fb9d) |
| Concurrency 7 | 0.9242, 0.9257, 0.9242 | 0.9295 (827fb9d), and 0.9242, 0.9265, 0.9303 (4f0fc5d) |

Two runs of the same code differ by up to 0.6 points, so the runs are pooled with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with one stratum a question. At concurrency 7, over the 3 runs on each side, this PR scores 0.23 points more than `main` (p 0.49, bootstrap 95% interval from 0.40 points less to 0.83 points more). Over all 5 runs of `main` and the 9 runs of this PR's versions, the mono path scores 0.14 points less (p 0.54, 95% interval from 0.65 points less to 0.36 points more). An earlier version of this description said 0.66 points less (p 0.05). That pool had `main`'s 2 runs at concurrency 1 only, and `main`'s 3 runs at concurrency 7 average 0.82 points below them. The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, as #60397's kernels and vLLM's gfx950 path do. vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.

**Kernel tests**, added by this PR and run by a new MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. All 240 pass on MI325X. The CPU test `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` passes too (51 tests).

| File | Tests | Compared against |
|---|---:|---|
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_topk.py` | 211 | vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode`, and vLLM's candidate mask followed by top-k. 1 and 3 requests with 5 drafts, 8 requests without drafts, contexts from 100 to 300,000 tokens. The index sets must be equal, except where values at the cut are equal. One more test checks that every hook leaves the step to vLLM when the build fails. |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_cand_logits.py` | 8 | AITER's dense Gluon logits at the candidate positions, bit for bit, for 32 and 64 heads. |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` | 3 | The old SWA metadata ops (causal and the DSpark draft block) and the old top-k packing, on 800 random batches. |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` | 6 | vLLM's Markov sampling loop, 1 and 2 requests at 3 temperatures. |
| `test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py` | 12 | Torch references for K2's key lists, the first layer's seam, the attention and MoE GEMV cores, the gfx942 FP4 and FP8 conversions, and the down stage's bf16 contributions at 42 rows, which must equal bf16(sum × route weight) bit for bit. |

**Layer by layer.** With `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW=1` (eager, block rejection), each mono layer runs and then vLLM's own layer runs on the same inputs, for the first 4 decode steps of each step width. 7 sanity prompts ran at once, so the steps had 42, 36, 30, 24, 18, 12 and 6 rows as the requests ended. All 43 layers reported: the 40 target layers and the 3 draft layers. No output has a non-finite value on any rank. The median relative norm of a standard layer's output difference is 4.1% at 6 rows and 4.5% to 5.8% at 12 to 42 rows. The index layers' top-512 lists match vLLM's in all 481,944 entries.

| Layers | Reports | `hidden_states` | `residual` | `post_mix`, `res_mix`, `pre_mix` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 and 1 (window) | 8 | 4.5% (11.8%) | 1.9% (2.1%) | 0.7% or less (1.0%) |
| 2 to 23 and 37 to 39 | 100 | 4.1% (19.7%) | 1.8% (3.2%) | 0.3% or less (1.6%) |

**Host syncs.** The PR arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, block rejection) through the sanity prompts and 100 GSM8K questions each at concurrency 1 and 8. Concurrency 8 makes steps of up to 48 rows, so it also covers the fallback to vLLM's path. No warning comes from the decode path or from a line this PR changes. All 207,200 warnings come from 4 lines of `combine_topk_swa_indices` in the image's prefill code at 81198e97, which this branch already replaces with a Triton version that does not sync.

**gfx950, compile only.** K1, K2 and the FFN launch were compiled for gfx950 before and after this PR (`ARCH=gfx950 COMPILE_ONLY=1`), at TP2 and TP4, 6 and 48 rows and compress ratios 1 and 2: 20 kernels. Every instruction count is the same except `s_waitcnt` (1 or 2 more or fewer) and `s_nop` (1 more in 2 kernels). VGPRs, LDS and scratch are the same. K1 takes 2 more kernel arguments, the index layers' outputs, and the FFN launch 1 more, its timeline buffer.

**API sanity.** Both arms answer "What is the capital of France?", an arithmetic chain and "Write hello world in C" correctly and in coherent text. With CUDA graphs and 7 concurrent prompts, in steps of up to 42 rows, the PR's 7 replies are correct and coherent.

## Details

### What this PR changes

- **The mono kernels on CDNA3** (4a36cc4). gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8. The kernels compute the same layer with FNUZ FP8 MFMAs on their own copies of the dense weights and dequantize the FP4 experts in VALU. The FP4 and FP8 weight bits do not change.
- **More layers take mono launches than on gfx950.** The window layers 0 and 1 run whole. The 8 index layers run K1, then vLLM's compressor and indexer, then K2. The 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch. On gfx950 the window and index layers run vLLM's attention and then the FFN launch, and the draft layers run vLLM's path.
- **Steps of up to 42 rows** (2dd3ff8). A GEMV pass takes 6 tokens, so that its x rows fit in 64 KB of LDS, and a step of 12 to 42 rows runs up to 7 passes on weights loaded once.
- **gfx942 ops around the mono launches:** the indexer's decode top-512 and candidate logits (d14f7e7), the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each (628c987), and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step (cfab906).
- **Load and reload** (f5994b7, 4f0fc5d). The gfx942 copies of the weights are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold the addresses of the first copies.

<details>
<summary>Commit by commit</summary>

| Commit | Change | Runs when | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4a36cc4 | The mono kernels built for CDNA3. gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8, so the kernels compute the same layer with FNUZ FP8 MFMAs on their own copies of the dense weights (`mono/weights942.py`) and dequantize the FP4 experts in VALU. The FP4 and FP8 weight bits do not change. The mono path also covers more of the other layers than #60397 does on gfx950. There, layers 0 and 1 and the 8 index layers run vLLM's attention and then the FFN launch, and the draft layers run vLLM's path. On gfx942 the window layers 0 and 1 run whole, the 8 index layers run K1, then vLLM's compressor and indexer, then K2, and the 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch. | gfx942, TP4, at most 6 rows (42 since 2dd3ff8) | vLLM's layer |
| d14f7e7 | The sparse indexer's decode top-512 as a gfx942 build of vLLM's top-512 kernel. Layer 20 writes the candidate blocks in one launch. Layers 24 to 36 compute only the 2048 × 8 candidate logits of a row and take the top 512 from those. An all-decode step skips the -1 fill of the top-k rows. | gfx942, any decode row count | vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` and dense logits |
| 628c987 | The SWA decode metadata (8 kernels for each of 8 SWA groups) and the global top-k packing (4 kernels for each of 8 index layers) as one Triton launch each. | at most 32 rows (SWA metadata), at most 16 rows (packing) | the old ops |
| cfab906 | DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step instead of about 9 kernels, in Model Runner V2's DSpark speculator. | at most 8 requests | vLLM's loop |
| bad4d75 | The `wvSplitK` skinny GEMM takes at most 4 rows on gfx942. `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` pads in rounds of 1024 instead of the step's block size. | see the next section | |
| fd7da16 | Triton imports through `vllm.triton_utils`, clang-format and mypy. | | |
| 983ec3b | The kernel tests and the MI300 CI job. | | |
| 2dd3ff8 | Steps of up to 42 rows on gfx942. A GEMV pass takes 6 tokens instead of 16 (`TILE`), so that its x rows fit in 64 KB of LDS, and a step of 12 to 42 rows runs 2 to 7 passes on weights loaded once. An ug task takes the picks of its own pick tile only. The gfx942 down stage still takes 16 picks a pass, because it reads its operands from global memory, and its second pass takes opaque copies of the weight words, without which the kernels spill from 18 rows. The down stage stores each contribution times its route weight as bf16, two rows a word, which `down_combine` rounded to bf16 before anyway, and `pair` holds one token tile. K2 and the FFN launch take 64,224 bytes of LDS and 218 to 224 VGPRs at 42 rows, with no scratch. The gfx950 kernels compile to the same ISA as on 983ec3b. The shadow check reports each step width. | gfx942, TP4, 12 to 42 rows | vLLM's layer |
| bdb26b8 | The merge of #60397's head 9a24c32a17. Its new check of the MoE backend is skipped on gfx942, because the gfx942 kernels read their own copies of the experts. | | |
| 09947e9 | `MonoLayerWeights.check_942` checks the gfx942 copies of the MoE weights before the kernels read them, as #60397's check does on gfx950. The CPU test of `mono_decode` passes on this branch and covers gfx942. | gfx942 | |
| 174d397 | `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built when the model is created instead of at the first decode step. When the build fails, the top-k hooks leave every step to vLLM's ops. | gfx942 | vLLM's top-k ops |
| 06007b2 | The opt-in fails at startup when the `ARCH` environment variable makes FlyDSL compile for another architecture than the GPU's, because the kernels follow `ARCH` and the choice of the gfx942 copies follows the GPU. | `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` | |
| f5994b7 | The gfx942 copies of the dense linears are made when vLLM processes the weights at load instead of at the first decode step, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. | gfx942 | |
| 4f0fc5d | Reloaded weights reach the gfx942 copies. vLLM's layerwise reload runs `process_weights_after_loading` again, and the copies it makes are then written into the first copies in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold the addresses of the first copies. A CPU test checks it. A reload was not run on a server. | gfx942, on a reload | |
| 2d52951 | Comments and docstrings only. They name the functions and kernels they mean, describe the code as it is, and correct a few wrong statements, for example that vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` also writes the -1 past a short row's end. | | |
| 67206b7 | An assert fixes the mypy error of f5994b7, and two docstrings no longer stop the strict docs build. No behavior change. | | |

</details>

The commits add 5,536 lines in 32 files outside tests, and 1,753 lines of tests and their CI job. The largest file is `topk512_gfx942.cu` (1,517 lines), which carries 524 lines of vLLM's top-k helpers unchanged.

### Changes outside the switch

- `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`: on gfx942 the `wvSplitK` skinny GEMM now takes at most 4 rows, for every model. At 5 rows it read the DSpark draft's 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard at 1.1 TB/s (297 µs, against 91 µs on hipBLASLt). Only that shape was measured. Other 5-row unquantized GEMMs on gfx942 now also run on hipBLASLt.
- `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`: the padding loops step 1,024 entries at a time instead of the step's block size, on every platform. They write the same values. It took about 44 µs a call on MI325X. It was not measured on other platforms.

### Memory

The gfx942 kernels read their own copies of the weights: the routed experts in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. vLLM keeps its own tensors for prefill and for the steps that run its path. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB (+71.23 GiB). On MI325X (256 GiB) with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache gets 28.59 GiB instead of 100.0 GiB, 11.18 million tokens instead of 39.11 million, which still holds 10 requests of 1M tokens. Before f5994b7 the dense copies were made in the first decode step, inside vLLM's memory profile, and the KV cache got 27.77 GiB (10.86 million tokens). MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well. Before f5994b7 the server did not start at 0.9, and at 0.955, about the most that is free at worker startup, the KV cache held 149K tokens. So the numbers and the recipe of this PR are for MI325X. Most of the 71 GiB are the routed-expert copies (about 69 GiB). One copy of the experts would remove them, see Follow-ups.

### Notes

- `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created, because the installed `vllm` package has no `csrc`. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops. Its helpers are vLLM's `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu` lines 48 to 571, unchanged.
- `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW=1` is a debugging aid for eager steps. It runs vLLM's own layer after each mono layer, logs how far apart the outputs are, and continues with vLLM's outputs.
- Every TP rank takes the same path at every layer, as in #60397, because the kernels wait on each other's pushes.

### Follow-ups

- Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 DSpark drafts also take the mono path. This needs to be fixed, and we are working on it. At 48 rows the shared expert has 288 units for 256 CTAs, so some CTAs have to run two. At high concurrency vLLM's path may be faster, so the largest step that takes the mono path should come from measurements.
- One copy of the routed experts instead of two, for example with vLLM's prefill MoE reading the gfx942 copies.
- Other TP sizes on gfx942. Only TP4 is built and tested.
- `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled vLLM op in `csrc/` instead of an extension built at startup.
- The two changes outside the switch as their own small PRs.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Cursor). The test commands and their results are under Validation and Reproduce.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

merged. Please rebase the PR, @maeehart.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

_Preliminary AI-assisted review. The analysis and testing were done with Claude Code (Opus 5.5 and GLM 5.3); I reviewed the results._

_As on #60397, this is an actively developing area, so these are suggestions ranked by how strongly I'd recommend them, not a checklist. The #60397 review comments carry over here and aren't repeated; its author has since pushed the deployment checks and test hardening there (dea9fa3b95, b9423a8c7d), which this branch doesn't have yet._

Thanks for this, and for the very thorough description. Tested on **MI300X** (192 GiB, 4 GPUs): this branch installed into `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-8cbd5d0300` (covers the merge-base). All 237 new gfx942 kernel tests pass on MI300X. E2E with the description's server command, adapted (block rejection, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 96`):

| | mono off | mono on |
|---|---|---|
| Weights per rank | 98.88 GiB | 169.07 GiB |
| KV cache | 63.79 GiB, 4.15M tokens (util 0.9) | **fails at util 0.9** (−8.25 GiB); 2.31 GiB, 149K tokens at 0.955 |
| Single request, 512 tokens, mean ITL | 6.10 ms | 2.70 ms (2.26×) |
| Kernels per decode period (torch profiler, rank 0) | 1,885 | 342; K1 ~24 µs, K2 93–97 µs, draft FFN launch 52 µs |
| GSM8K 5-shot, first 400, greedy, concurrency 1 | 0.930 ± 0.013 | 0.950 ± 0.011 |

So the speedup, kernel counts and accuracy match the description on MI300X too.

### Would like to see before merge

**1. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is JIT-built with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load` at the first decode step.** vLLM builds its kernels through `csrc/` and CMake; a runtime hipcc build needs hipcc and a writable extension cache at serve time, fails mid-serving instead of at startup, and has no fallback. Please move it into `csrc/` (or at least build at startup with a fallback to `top_k_per_row_decode`).

**2. `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` fails 6 of 26 with this PR**, none of them hardware-dependent: the CDNA message is now "needs CDNA3/4", the mocks lack `layer.engram`, `runner.ffn()` takes `topk`, and a path needs the TP group. It runs in the MI355 Basic Models step, so CI goes red once it runs.

**3. MI300X doesn't really fit.** With the copies, the description's own `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` fails at startup on MI300X; the ceiling is ~0.955 (only ~184 of 192 GiB free at worker startup), leaving 2.31 GiB of KV — 149K tokens, about two 64K requests, and not one at the recipe's 1M context. Most of the +70 GiB is the routed-expert copies (~69 GiB). I'd scope the claims to MI325X, or document the MI300X limits.

**4. The rebase onto #60397's new head needs care.** The parent's new `MonoLayerWeights.check` asserts the gfx950 layout (fp4x2 `w13`, E8M0 block scales, padded intermediate); on gfx942 the tensors are the `weights942` copies (FNUZ bytes, tile-major, padding cut), so the check needs a gfx942 variant or the copies go unchecked — the exact gap the parent's fix closed. The unit test file also changed there (new MoE-rejection and padded-step cases), so it's a reconcile, not just fixing the 6 failures.

### Recommended, fine as follow-ups

**5. Reloaded weights don't reach the copies.** `_capture_plain_experts` skips the rebuild when `mono942` exists, and the dense copies are cached on first use, so after `reload_weights` or an RL weight update, prefill uses the new weights while ≤6-row decode silently uses the old ones. Captured graphs hold the copies' pointers, so a fix would `copy_` into them in place.

**6. The two changes outside the switch** (the `wvSplitK` ≤4 rows on gfx942 for every model, and the DFlash padding on every platform) each have a single measurement behind them. They'd be easier to land and to bisect as their own small PRs.

### Nits

- The dense copies (~1.8 GiB) are built at the first eager decode step, which by default is the cudagraph memory-profiling pass, so they're counted as graph memory (estimate 5.74 GiB with mono vs 3.40 without). That works, but only by accident: with graph-memory profiling off or `enforce_eager` they'd escape accounting. Building them at load would be clearer.
- `common/arch.py` decides `GFX942` from the `ARCH` env var, while `_on_gfx942()` asks the platform. A stray `ARCH` (a generic name) can make the weight copies and the kernel builds disagree.
- A gfx942 twin of the parent's new 300-replay graph stress (both widths, one graph, bit for bit) would guard the FNUZ copies' path; the shadow mode (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW`) already provides the harness.

For what it's worth, the FNUZ re-encoding traced as exact: the bf16 → e4m3 round trip, the halved bit patterns with scale code +1, subnormals and −0. The checkpoint's scale codes (dense 109–121, experts 115–127) are well clear of the E8M0 edge cases.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, as in #60397. No other open PR ports these kernels to gfx942.

The PR is stacked on #60397 and merges its head 9a24c32a17. Its own commits are the 8 after 73f40ed and the 7 after that merge. Until #60397 merges, the diff against `main` includes #60397.

**Speculative decoding works at every concurrency.** The mono path takes decode steps of up to 42 rows on gfx942, which is up to 7 concurrent requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A step of 8 or more requests runs vLLM's path, with the same speculative decoding, and gets none of the speedup. That limit needs to be fixed, and we are working on it (see Follow-ups).

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, 5 DSpark drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points, because there is no `main` run at these concurrencies: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×). Total throughput per GPU goes from 4,255 to 6,729 tokens/s (1.58×), from 6,315 to 8,882 (1.41×) and from 10,998 to 14,839 (1.35×).
- A standard decoder layer runs as 2 kernels instead of 32, in 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` averages 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 (pooled p 0.49). Over all 5 runs of `main` and the 9 runs of this PR's versions, the mono path is 0.14 points lower (p 0.54). Neither difference is significant. The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, where vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.
- gfx950 is unchanged. A compile-only gfx950 build of the 20 kernels before and after this PR gives the same instruction counts, apart from 1 or 2 `s_waitcnt` and `s_nop`. No MI355X was used.
- The gfx942 kernels run only with the switch on, on gfx942. Two small changes apply without the switch, see "Changes outside the switch".

## Requirements of the gfx942 mono path

Mono kernels are built for fixed shapes. A deployment or a step outside these limits runs vLLM's own path.

| | gfx942 (this PR) | gfx950 (#60397) |
|---|---|---|
| Tensor parallel size | 4 | 2 or 4 |
| Rows a decode step, requests × (1 + drafts) | at most 42 | at most 48 |
| Concurrency with 5 DSpark drafts | up to 7 | up to 8 |
| Concurrency without drafts | up to 40 with FULL CUDA graphs, 42 in eager mode | up to 48 |
| Steps | decode only, eager or a FULL CUDA graph | same |
| KV cache | `fp8_ds_mla` | same |
| MoE | DeepSeek-V4.1 routing: 384 experts, top 6, sqrtsoftplus, ×1.5, a shared expert. The draft layers use 128 experts and top 3. | same, no draft layers |

- The row limit comes from LDS. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950. So a gfx942 GEMV pass holds the x rows of 6 tokens instead of 16, and a step of 12 to 42 rows runs 2 to 7 passes on weights loaded once.
- A FULL CUDA graph step runs padded to the next graph size, and the mono path takes the padded step. With 5 DSpark drafts the graph sizes are 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 42 and 48 rows, so a step of 5 requests runs as 36 rows.
- At TP2 on gfx942 the path logs one line, and every layer runs vLLM's path. A TP size other than 2 or 4 is an error at startup, as in #60397.
- A step outside the limits, for example prefill, a mixed step, more than 42 rows or a PIECEWISE graph, runs vLLM's path on every layer and every rank. Both paths take and return the same tensors at each layer, so the engine can switch between them from one step to the next.

## Validation

**Setup.** MI325X, TP4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`. Both arms use one image, one command and one environment, listed under Reproduce. They differ only in the `vllm` package and in `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE`.

- `main`: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` as it is (vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev88+g81198e97b, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1, amd-aiter 0.1.24.post1).
- PR: the same image, with the `vllm/` changes of #60397 and this PR copied over its `vllm` package (see Reproduce). The changes that came into this branch with `main` and #60397 after 242e4213 are not in the PR arm.

### AgentX, concurrency 1, against `main`

One 3,600 s run per arm, each on a fresh server, with the InferenceX AgentX client. Interactivity is 1 / the inter-token latency, so P90 is the slow tail. Throughput is the input and output tokens of the measured requests over the run time, divided by the 4 GPUs.

| | `main` | PR | PR / `main` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured requests, no errors | 239 | 306 | |
| Interactivity P50 (tokens/s/user) | 216.85 | 503.53 | 2.32× |
| Interactivity P90 (tokens/s/user) | 182.25 | 411.26 | 2.26× |
| Interactivity mean (tokens/s/user) | 200.43 | 461.94 | 2.30× |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 0.510 | 0.544 | |
| Total throughput per GPU (tokens/s) | 4,024 | 6,546 | 1.63× |

- Concurrency 1 is one recorded Claude Code session at a time, not one request at a time. When the recorded agent ran subagents in parallel, the replay sends their requests at the same time. 34 of the PR's 305 requests overlap another request, in steps of 12 or 18 rows, and take the mono path too. Their median interactivity is 392, against 178 on `main`.
- All 239 requests of the `main` run are also in the PR run, with the same output lengths. On those, the PR's inter-token latency is 0.429× `main`'s at the median (P10 0.420, P90 0.450).
- The PR run is from an earlier version of 2dd3ff8 that took steps of up to 30 rows. Its decode TPOT at steps of 6, 12 and 18 rows is 1.86, 2.46 and 3.21 ms, against 1.86, 2.38 and 3.10 ms on 2dd3ff8.

### AgentX, concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points

There is no `main` run at these concurrencies. The published points are InferenceX's MI325X AgentX results at TP4 from [Actions run 35637516947](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35637516947), with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984` and InferenceX's own recipe. That is an older nightly, so it stands in for `main` only roughly. At concurrency 1 the published point is close to our `main` run: P90 189.90 against 182.25, and 3,913 against 4,024 tokens/s per GPU.

Interactivity is in tokens/s/user, TTFT in seconds and throughput in tokens/s per GPU. The ratios are against the published point at the same concurrency.

| Concurrency | Run | Measured requests, no errors | Interactivity P50 | Interactivity P90 | Interactivity mean | TTFT P50 | Total throughput per GPU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | Published | 378 | 215.71 | 153.22 | 170.09 | 0.653 | 4,255 |
| 2 | PR, 2dd3ff8 | 493 | 501.98 (2.33×) | 368.64 (2.41×) | 400.82 (2.36×) | 0.417 | 6,729 (1.58×) |
| 4 | Published | 539 | 196.51 | 142.75 | 159.96 | 0.537 | 6,315 |
| 4 | PR, 06007b2 | 673 | 491.35 (2.50×) | 316.28 (2.22×) | 379.47 (2.37×) | 0.369 | 8,882 (1.41×) |
| 8 | Published | 1,112 | 146.76 | 81.52 | 120.31 | 0.514 | 10,998 |
| 8 | PR, 06007b2 | 1,373 | 317.99 (2.17×) | 162.61 (1.99×) | 258.60 (2.15×) | 0.397 | 14,839 (1.35×) |

- At concurrency 2 at most 3 requests decoded at once, and at concurrency 4 at most 5. So every decode step had at most 30 rows, 36 with the graph padding, and took the mono path.
- At concurrency 8 at most 8 requests decoded at once. Steps of more than 42 rows run vLLM's path, and they took 0.14% of the time with any request decoding. 1 request decoded during 45.6% of that time, 2 during 27.2%, 3 during 15.4% and 4 or more during 11.8%.
- Requests that decoded alone have an interactivity P50 of 509, 508 and 511 at concurrency 2, 4 and 8. Requests that overlapped another request have a median of 390, 386 and 299.

### What runs on each layer

Torch profiler on rank 0, 40 engine steps under AgentX traffic, each step 1 request with 6 rows. The numbers are medians over 39 decode periods on `main` and 35 on the PR. A period runs from the start of one decode step to the start of the next, so it includes the lm_head, sampling and the DSpark drafter. The profile is of the first version of this PR (983ec3b), which took steps of 6 rows only.

| | `main` | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode period (ms) | 17.92 | 7.20 |
| Target forward (ms) | 15.85 | 5.98 |
| Kernels in a period | 1,901 | 340 |
| Kernels in layers 0 to 39 | 1,581 | 180 |
| GPU time after the forward: lm_head, sampling, DSpark drafter (ms) | 2.03 | 1.18 |

<details>
<summary>Each layer type, a standard layer part by part, and the timelines</summary>

| Layers | Layer type | Kernels a layer, `main` | Kernels a layer, PR | GPU time a layer, `main` (µs) | GPU time a layer, PR (µs) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | window only, first layer | 172 | 9 | 941 | 172 |
| 1 | window only, Engram | 40 | 9 | 417 | 205 |
| 2, 8 | index | 48 | 14 | 485 | 236 |
| 14 | index, Engram | 55 | 21 | 557 | 318 |
| 20 | index, writes the candidate blocks | 64 | 15 | 621 | 322 |
| 24, 28, 32, 36 | index, candidate logits | 47 | 8 | 532 | 167 |
| the 27 standard layers from 3 to 36 | standard | 32 | 2 | 320 | 115 |
| 37, 38, 39 | standard, hidden states kept for DSpark | 34 | 4 | 335 | 133 |

- On `main`, 141 of layer 0's 172 kernels are small elementwise and reduce kernels. The folded form of the first layer's entry seam has no AITER kernel on gfx942, so it runs the eager reference. With this PR, layer 0 runs as a whole mono layer and takes the unfolded form, which AITER's fused seam kernel covers.
- What still runs outside the mono launches with this PR: the Engram lookup and projection (layers 0, 1 and 14), vLLM's compressor and indexer on the index layers with the gfx942 top-512 and key list, and vLLM's mHC post and mean before layers 37 to 39, which make the hidden states the drafter reads.
- After the forward, the 5 Markov steps of the drafter take 1 launch each (5 × about 18 µs) instead of about 9 kernels each, and the 3 draft layers end in `dsv41_mono_ffn` (about 50 µs each).

A standard layer, one of the 30 (3 to 7, 9 to 13, 15 to 19, 21 to 23, 25 to 27, 29 to 31, 33 to 35, 37 to 39). The `main` column is layer 5 of one period.

| Part of the layer | Kernels on `main` | GPU time on `main` (µs) | With this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Attention seam: mHC pre and the RMSNorm | 5 | 26 | K1, 23 µs |
| Attention front: wqkv, the q and KV norms, wq_b, the KV insert | 4 | 28 | K1 |
| Sparse attention: split attention and combine | 2 | 40 | K2, 89 µs |
| Attention back: wo_a and wo_b, with a copy and an elementwise kernel | 4 | 30 | K2 |
| Attention all-reduce | 1 | 8 | K2, in-kernel over peer memory |

### Accuracy

**GSM8K.** `lm_eval` `gsm8k` (the stock task), 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, greedy, at most 512 new tokens, through `/v1/completions`. Both arms use DSpark block rejection for these runs, so the target model checks every draft token. At concurrency 7 the steps have 6 to 42 rows, and with this PR all of them take the mono path. Strict-match of each run:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1 | 0.9340, 0.9318 | 0.9272 (827fb9d) |
| Concurrency 7 | 0.9242, 0.9257, 0.9242 | 0.9295 (827fb9d), and 0.9242, 0.9265, 0.9303 (4f0fc5d) |

Two runs of the same code differ by up to 0.6 points, so the runs are pooled with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with one stratum a question. At concurrency 7, over the 3 runs on each side, this PR scores 0.23 points more than `main` (p 0.49, bootstrap 95% interval from 0.40 points less to 0.83 points more). Over all 5 runs of `main` and the 9 runs of this PR's versions, the mono path scores 0.14 points less (p 0.54, 95% interval from 0.65 points less to 0.36 points more). An earlier version of this description said 0.66 points less (p 0.05). That pool had `main`'s 2 runs at concurrency 1 only, and `main`'s 3 runs at concurrency 7 average 0.82 points below them. The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, as #60397's kernels and vLLM's gfx950 path do. vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.

**Kernel tests**, added by this PR and run by a new MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. All 240 pass on MI325X. The CPU test `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` passes too (51 tests).

The index sets must be equal, except where values at the cut are equal. One more test checks that every hook leaves the step to vLLM when the build fails. |

All 43 layers reported: the 40 target layers and the 3 draft layers. No output has a non-finite value on any rank. The median relative norm of a standard layer's output difference is 4.1% at 6 rows and 4.5% to 5.8% at 12 to 42 rows. The index layers' top-512 lists match vLLM's in all 481,944 entries.

**Host syncs.** The PR arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, block rejection) through the sanity prompts and 100 GSM8K questions each at concurrency 1 and 8. Concurrency 8 makes steps of up to 48 rows, so it also covers the fallback to vLLM's path. No warning comes from the decode path or from a line this PR changes. All 207,200 warnings come from 4 lines of `combine_topk_swa_indices` in the image's prefill code at 81198e97, which this branch already replaces with a Triton version that does not sync.

**gfx950, compile only.** K1, K2 and the FFN launch were compiled for gfx950 before and after this PR (`ARCH=gfx950 COMPILE_ONLY=1`), at TP2 and TP4, 6 and 48 rows and compress ratios 1 and 2: 20 kernels. Every instruction count is the same except `s_waitcnt` (1 or 2 more or fewer) and `s_nop` (1 more in 2 kernels). VGPRs, LDS and scratch are the same. K1 takes 2 more kernel arguments, the index layers' outputs, and the FFN launch 1 more, its timeline buffer.

**API sanity.** Both arms answer "What is the capital of France?", an arithmetic chain and "Write hello world in C" correctly and in coherent text. With CUDA graphs and 7 concurrent prompts, in steps of up to 42 rows, the PR's 7 replies are correct and coherent.

## Details

### What this PR changes

- **The mono kernels on CDNA3** (4a36cc4). gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8. The kernels compute the same layer with FNUZ FP8 MFMAs on their own copies of the dense weights and dequantize the FP4 experts in VALU. The FP4 and FP8 weight bits do not change.
- **More layers take mono launches than on gfx950.** The window layers 0 and 1 run whole. The 8 index layers run K1, then vLLM's compressor and indexer, then K2. The 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch. On gfx950 the window and index layers run vLLM's attention and then the FFN launch, and the draft layers run vLLM's path.
- **Steps of up to 42 rows** (2dd3ff8). A GEMV pass takes 6 tokens, so that its x rows fit in 64 KB of LDS, and a step of 12 to 42 rows runs up to 7 passes on weights loaded once.
- **gfx942 ops around the mono launches:** the indexer's decode top-512 and candidate logits (d14f7e7), the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each (628c987), and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step (cfab906).
- **Load and reload** (f5994b7, 4f0fc5d). The gfx942 copies of the weights are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold the addresses of the first copies.

The commits add 5,536 lines in 32 files outside tests, and 1,753 lines of tests and their CI job. The largest file is `topk512_gfx942.cu` (1,517 lines), which carries 524 lines of vLLM's top-k helpers unchanged.

### Changes outside the switch

- `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`: on gfx942 the `wvSplitK` skinny GEMM now takes at most 4 rows, for every model. At 5 rows it read the DSpark draft's 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard at 1.1 TB/s (297 µs, against 91 µs on hipBLASLt). Only that shape was measured. Other 5-row unquantized GEMMs on gfx942 now also run on hipBLASLt.
- `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`: the padding loops step 1,024 entries at a time instead of the step's block size, on every platform. They write the same values. It took about 44 µs a call on MI325X. It was not measured on other platforms.

### Memory

The gfx942 kernels read their own copies of the weights: the routed experts in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. vLLM keeps its own tensors for prefill and for the steps that run its path. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB (+71.23 GiB). On MI325X (256 GiB) with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache gets 28.59 GiB instead of 100.0 GiB, 11.18 million tokens instead of 39.11 million, which still holds 10 requests of 1M tokens. Before f5994b7 the dense copies were made in the first decode step, inside vLLM's memory profile, and the KV cache got 27.77 GiB (10.86 million tokens). MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well. Before f5994b7 the server did not start at 0.9, and at 0.955, about the most that is free at worker startup, the KV cache held 149K tokens. So the numbers and the recipe of this PR are for MI325X. Most of the 71 GiB are the routed-expert copies (about 69 GiB). One copy of the experts would remove them, see Follow-ups.

### Notes

- `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created, because the installed `vllm` package has no `csrc`. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops. Its helpers are vLLM's `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu` lines 48 to 571, unchanged.
- `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW=1` is a debugging aid for eager steps. It runs vLLM's own layer after each mono layer, logs how far apart the outputs are, and continues with vLLM's outputs.
- Every TP rank takes the same path at every layer, as in #60397, because the kernels wait on each other's pushes.

### Follow-ups

- Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 DSpark drafts also take the mono path. This needs to be fixed, and we are working on it. At 48 rows the shared expert has 288 units for 256 CTAs, so some CTAs have to run two. At high concurrency vLLM's path may be faster, so the largest step that takes the mono path should come from measurements.
- One copy of the routed experts instead of two, for example with vLLM's prefill MoE reading the gfx942 copies.
- Other TP sizes on gfx942. Only TP4 is built and tested.
- `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled vLLM op in `csrc/` instead of an extension built at startup.
- The two changes outside the switch as their own small PRs.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""cand_logits.candidate_logits against AITER's dense
+deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits, called the way vLLM's decode indexer calls it
+on gfx942 (rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits).
+
+For one decode request of 6 rows, every compact logit and id must be
+bit-identical to the dense logit gathered at the same candidate position,
+with -inf and id -1 where a candidate block is -1 or a position is at or past
+the row's end. The top 512 of the compact rows must then be the top 512 that
+candidate_top_k_512 takes from the dense rows within the candidate blocks.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _on_gfx942(), reason="the kernel reproduces AITER's gfx942 kernel"
+)
+
+ROWS, DIM, PAGE = 6, 128, 64
+MAX_MODEL_LEN = 1 << 20
+CAND_BLOCKS, CAND_BLOCK = 2048, 8
+
+
+def _make_inputs(ctx: int, heads: int):
+    """FP8 queries, head weights, row lengths, block tables and a paged
+    indexer cache of FP8 keys and FP32 key scales. Row r is the request's
+    token at position ctx - ROWS + r and sees the keys up to its own
+    position."""
+    from aiter import dtypes
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    q = (torch.randn(ROWS, 1, heads, DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    weights = torch.randn(ROWS, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    context_lens = torch.arange(
+        ctx - ROWS + 1, ctx + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    used = (ctx + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    num_pages = used + 64
+    tables = torch.zeros(ROWS, MAX_MODEL_LEN // PAGE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    tables[:, :used] = torch.randperm(num_pages, device="cuda")[:used].to(torch.int32)
+    vals = (torch.randn(num_pages, PAGE * DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(dtypes.fp8)
+    scales = torch.rand(num_pages, PAGE, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    kv = torch.cat([vals.view(torch.uint8), scales.view(torch.uint8)], dim=1)
+    return q, weights, context_lens, tables, kv.view(num_pages, PAGE, 1, DIM + 4)
+
+
+def _make_candidates(context_lens: torch.Tensor, gen) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Distinct candidate blocks of each row in random order, with the row's
+    newest block among them and -1 padding where a row has fewer than 2048
+    blocks. Row 1 also gets -1 in a few places in the middle, as layer 20
+    writes for a block whose score is -inf."""
+    cand = torch.full((ROWS, CAND_BLOCKS), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for r in range(ROWS):
+        blocks = (int(context_lens[r]) + CAND_BLOCK - 1) // CAND_BLOCK
+        if blocks <= CAND_BLOCKS:
+            picks = torch.randperm(blocks, generator=gen)
+        else:
+            others = torch.randperm(blocks - 1, generator=gen)[: CAND_BLOCKS - 1]
+            picks = torch.cat([others, torch.tensor([blocks - 1])])
+            picks = picks[torch.randperm(CAND_BLOCKS, generator=gen)]
+        cand[r, : picks.numel()] = picks.to(torch.int32)
+    cand[1, 100:105] = -1
+    return cand.cuda()
+
+
+def _gather_reference(dense, context_lens, cand):
+    """The compact rows that gatherCandidates writes from dense logits."""
+    i = torch.arange(CAND_BLOCKS * CAND_BLOCK, device=cand.device)
+    block = cand[:, i // CAND_BLOCK].long()
+    col = block * CAND_BLOCK + (i % CAND_BLOCK)[None, :]
+    live = (block >= 0) & (col < context_lens[:, None].long())
+    logits = torch.gather(dense[:ROWS], 1, torch.where(live, col, 0))
+    logits = torch.where(live, logits, float("-inf"))
+    ids = torch.where(live, col, -1).to(torch.int32)
+    return logits, ids
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_lens_2d", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [32, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ctx", [8192, 131072])
+def test_candidate_logits_bit_identical_to_dense(ctx, heads, seq_lens_2d):
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.dsv41_gfx942 import cand_logits, topk
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import paged_mqa_logits_module
+
+    aiter_logits = paged_mqa_logits_module()
+    if aiter_logits is None:
+        pytest.skip("AITER's paged MQA logits module is not installed")
+    q, weights, context_lens, tables, kv = _make_inputs(ctx, heads)
+    cand = _make_candidates(context_lens.cpu(), torch.Generator().manual_seed(1))
+    lens = context_lens.view(-1, 1) if seq_lens_2d else context_lens
+    row_len = CAND_BLOCKS * CAND_BLOCK
+    dense = torch.full((ROWS, MAX_MODEL_LEN), -1.0, device="cuda")
+    out_logits = torch.empty(ROWS, row_len, device="cuda")
+    out_ids = torch.empty(ROWS, row_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    aiter_logits.deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(
+        q,
+        kv,
+        weights,
+        dense,
+        context_lens,
+        tables,
+        MAX_MODEL_LEN,
+        ChunkK=256,
+        Preshuffle=True,
+        KVBlockSize=PAGE,
+        WavePerEU=2,
+    )
+    cand_logits.candidate_logits(
+        q.view(ROWS, heads, DIM),
+        kv,
+        weights,
+        lens,
+        1,
+        tables,
+        cand,
+        CAND_BLOCK,
+        out_logits,
+        out_ids,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref_logits, ref_ids = _gather_reference(dense, context_lens, cand)
+    assert torch.equal(ref_ids, out_ids)
+    assert torch.equal(ref_logits.view(torch.int32), out_logits.view(torch.int32))
+
+    ext = topk._load()
+    old = torch.empty(ROWS, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    new = torch.empty_like(old)
+    ext.candidate_top_k_512(dense, 1, lens, cand, CAND_BLOCK, old)
+    ext.compact_top_k_512_regs(out_logits, out_ids, lens, 1, new)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(old.sort(1).values, new.sort(1).values)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The one-launch DeepSeek-V4.1 decode metadata of gfx942 against the vLLM
+ops that it replaces.
+
+swa_decode_meta.launch replaces the decode part of the ROCm SWA metadata
+build: torch.ge for is_valid_token, the zero fill of the unused lengths,
+_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel (or the DSpark draft block's
+ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel), build_ragged_indices_from_dense and
+_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers. topk_pack.launch replaces
+compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr. For each random decode batch
+vLLM's ops run first. Then every output buffer is overwritten with -7
+(is_valid_token with its negation), the fused launch runs, and every output
+that a reader uses must be equal.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="the fused launches are for ROCm"
+)
+
+WINDOW = 128
+MAX_TOKENS = 16384
+MAX_SEQS = 128
+TOPK = 512
+
+
+def _swa_case(g, max_rows):
+    """A random decode batch. It mixes short sequences, sequences at 128k,
+    padded tokens with slot -1, a replay start inside the window, null blocks
+    (block 0) and block sizes 64 and 128. Returns None when the batch has more
+    rows than the fused launch takes."""
+    block_size = (64, 128)[int(torch.randint(0, 2, (1,), generator=g))]
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, 6, (1,), generator=g))
+    q_len = (1, 6)[int(torch.randint(0, 2, (1,), generator=g))]
+    lens = []
+    for _ in range(num_reqs):
+        kind = int(torch.randint(0, 3, (1,), generator=g))
+        if kind == 0:
+            lens.append(int(torch.randint(q_len, 140, (1,), generator=g)))
+        elif kind == 1:
+            lens.append(int(torch.randint(140, 5000, (1,), generator=g)))
+        else:
+            lens.append(131072 + int(torch.randint(0, 64, (1,), generator=g)))
+    n = num_reqs * q_len
+    if n > max_rows:
+        return None
+    max_blocks = (max(lens) + block_size - 1) // block_size + 1
+    block_table = torch.randint(
+        1, 200000, (MAX_SEQS, max_blocks), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    # The sliding window manager points blocks outside the window at the
+    # null block 0. Put some of those inside windows as well.
+    block_table[torch.rand(block_table.shape, generator=g) < 0.05] = 0
+    slot_mapping = torch.randint(0, 1 << 30, (n,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int64)
+    slot_mapping[torch.rand(n, generator=g) < 0.15] = -1
+    replay = torch.zeros(MAX_SEQS + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for r in range(num_reqs):
+        if float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.3:
+            replay[r] = max(0, lens[r] - int(torch.randint(1, 160, (1,), generator=g)))
+    return dict(
+        n=n,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        slot_mapping=slot_mapping.cuda(),
+        query_start_loc=(torch.arange(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32) * q_len).cuda(),
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32).cuda(),
+        token_to_req=(torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32) // q_len).cuda(),
+        block_table=block_table.cuda(),
+        replay_start=replay.cuda(),
+    )
+
+
+def _swa_buffers(width, noncausal):
+    """Buffers of the size that the metadata builder allocates."""
+    return dict(
+        noncausal=noncausal,
+        width=width,
+        is_valid=torch.zeros(MAX_TOKENS, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"),
+        indices=torch.zeros(MAX_TOKENS, 1, width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        lens=torch.full((MAX_TOKENS,), 5, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        ragged=torch.empty(MAX_TOKENS * width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        indptr=torch.empty(MAX_TOKENS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+    )
+
+
+def _swa_old_ops(c, b):
+    """The decode part of vLLM's SWA metadata build and its ROCm ragged
+    step."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm import _copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.sparse_swa import (
+        _COMPUTE_DSPARK_NONCAUSAL_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL,
+        _COMPUTE_SWA_INDICES_AND_LENS_KERNEL,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        build_ragged_indices_from_dense,
+    )
+
+    n, width = c["n"], b["width"]
+    is_valid = b["is_valid"][:n]
+    torch.ge(c["slot_mapping"], 0, out=is_valid)
+    b["lens"][n:] = 0
+    common = (c["query_start_loc"], c["seq_lens"], c["token_to_req"], is_valid)
+    if b["noncausal"]:
+        _COMPUTE_DSPARK_NONCAUSAL_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL(
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            WINDOW,
+            width,
+            *common,
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["block_size"],
+            num_tokens=n,
+            token_offset=0,
+        )
+    else:
+        _COMPUTE_SWA_INDICES_AND_LENS_KERNEL(
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            WINDOW,
+            width,
+            b["lens"],
+            b["lens"],
+            *common,
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["block_size"],
+            c["replay_start"],
+            num_tokens=n,
+            token_offset=0,
+        )
+    ragged, indptr = build_ragged_indices_from_dense(
+        b["indices"][:n].reshape(n, width), b["lens"][:n]
+    )
+    _copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers(ragged, indptr, b["ragged"], b["indptr"], n, width)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("noncausal", [False, True])
+def test_swa_decode_meta_matches_vllm_ops(noncausal):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import swa_decode_meta
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.compressor_utils import (
+        get_dspark_swa_index_width,
+    )
+
+    width = get_dspark_swa_index_width(WINDOW, 5) if noncausal else WINDOW
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1234)
+    failed, done = [], 0
+    while done < 300:
+        c = _swa_case(g, swa_decode_meta.MAX_ROWS)
+        if c is None:
+            continue
+        done += 1
+        n = c["n"]
+        b = _swa_buffers(width, noncausal)
+        _swa_old_ops(c, b)
+        nnz = int(b["indptr"][n])
+        want = dict(
+            is_valid=b["is_valid"][:n].clone(),
+            indices=b["indices"][:n].clone(),
+            lens=b["lens"].clone(),
+            indptr=b["indptr"][: n + 1].clone(),
+            ragged=b["ragged"][:nnz].clone(),
+        )
+        b["is_valid"][:n].copy_(~want["is_valid"])
+        for key in ("indices", "lens", "ragged", "indptr"):
+            b[key].fill_(-7)
+        swa_decode_meta.launch(
+            c["slot_mapping"],
+            b["is_valid"][:n],
+            b["indices"],
+            b["lens"],
+            b["ragged"],
+            b["indptr"],
+            c["query_start_loc"],
+            c["seq_lens"],
+            c["token_to_req"],
+            c["block_table"],
+            c["replay_start"],
+            n,
+            WINDOW,
+            c["block_size"],
+            noncausal=noncausal,
+        )
+        got = dict(
+            is_valid=b["is_valid"][:n],
+            indices=b["indices"][:n],
+            lens=b["lens"],
+            indptr=b["indptr"][: n + 1],
+            ragged=b["ragged"][:nnz],
+        )
+        bad = [k for k in want if not torch.equal(want[k], got[k])]
+        if bad:
+            failed.append((done, n, c["block_size"], bad))
+    assert not failed, (
+        f"batches that differ (case, rows, block size, outputs): {failed}"
+    )
+
+
+def _topk_case(g, max_rows):
+    """A decode batch of top-512 rows as the indexer writes them: valid local
+    indices first and -1 after them, some rows shorter than 512, some rows
+    with a -1 inside the valid entries, and padded tokens."""
+    n = int(torch.randint(1, max_rows + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, n + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    block_size = (32, 64, 128)[int(torch.randint(0, 3, (1,), generator=g))]
+    comp_len = int(torch.randint(1, 70000, (1,), generator=g))
+    blocks = (comp_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
+    block_table = torch.randint(
+        0, 300000, (MAX_SEQS, blocks + 1), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    topk = torch.full((n, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for t in range(n):
+        valid = min(TOPK, int(torch.randint(0, comp_len + 1, (1,), generator=g)))
+        if float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.5:
+            valid = min(TOPK, comp_len)
+        topk[t, :valid] = torch.randperm(comp_len, generator=g)[:valid].to(torch.int32)
+        if valid > 4 and float(torch.rand(1, generator=g)) < 0.2:
+            topk[t, int(torch.randint(0, valid, (1,), generator=g))] = -1
+    t2r = torch.sort(torch.randint(0, num_reqs, (n,), generator=g)).values
+    is_valid = torch.rand(n, generator=g) > 0.15
+    return (
+        topk.cuda(),
+        t2r.to(torch.int32).cuda(),
+        block_table.cuda(),
+        block_size,
+        is_valid.cuda(),
+    )
+
+
+def test_topk_pack_matches_vllm():
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd import rocm, topk_pack
+
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(4321)
+    failed = []
+    for i in range(500):
+        case = _topk_case(g, topk_pack.MAX_ROWS)
+        ref = rocm._compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr_old(*case)
+        out = topk_pack.launch(*case, poison=True)
+        nnz = int(ref[1][-1])
+        bad = [
+            name
+            for name, a, b in (
+                ("topk_lens", out[2], ref[2]),
+                ("topk_indptr", out[1], ref[1]),
+                ("global_topk_ragged", out[0][:nnz], ref[0][:nnz]),
+            )
+            if a.shape != b.shape or not torch.equal(a, b)
+        ]
+        if out[0].shape != ref[0].shape:
+            bad.append("ragged shape")
+        if bad:
+            failed.append((i, case[0].shape[0], bad))
+    assert not failed, f"batches that differ (case, rows, outputs): {failed}"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""fused_markov.sample_sequential against vLLM's
+DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential.
+
+Both paths run on the same random Markov head, base logits and sampling
+state, for 1 and 2 requests at temperatures 0, 0.6 and 1.0. vLLM's bias is
+the server's GEMV (rocm_unquantized_gemm). The fused launch adds the bias's
+256 products in another order, so a bias value can differ in its last bf16
+bit, and then a draft token can differ. That changes only what the draft
+proposes, because the rejection sampler checks every draft token against the
+target. So the test allows at most 1 in 1000 cached logits to differ, and a
+draft token may differ only when a cached logit differed.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="the fused launch is for ROCm"
+)
+
+VOCAB, RANK, N_SPEC, MAX_REQS = 129280, 256, 5, 4
+
+
+def _set_gate(monkeypatch, on: bool):
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.dsv41_gfx942 import enabled
+
+    if on:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE", "1")
+    else:
+        monkeypatch.delenv("VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE", raising=False)
+    enabled.cache_clear()
+
+
+class _MarkovW2(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, w):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+            UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+        )
+
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+        self.quant_method = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+
+
+class _Model:
+    """The parts of the DSpark draft model that the sampling uses. The base
+    logits are fixed, so both paths sample from the same ones."""
+
+    def __init__(self, w1, w2, base):
+        head = torch.nn.Module()
+        head.markov_w1 = torch.nn.Embedding(VOCAB, RANK, _weight=w1)
+        head.markov_w2 = _MarkovW2(w2)
+        self.model = SimpleNamespace(markov_head=head)
+        self.base = base
+
+    def compute_draft_logits(self, hidden):
+        return self.base[: hidden.shape[0]]
+
+    def markov_embed(self, ids):
+        return self.model.markov_head.markov_w1(ids)
+
+    def markov_bias(self, e):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import rocm_unquantized_gemm
+
+        w2 = self.model.markov_head.markov_w2
+        return rocm_unquantized_gemm(w2, e, w2.weight, None)
+
+    def map_draft_to_target(self, ids):
+        return ids
+
+
+def _speculator(temp: float, seed: int):
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.speculator import DSparkSpeculator
+
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    bf16 = torch.bfloat16
+    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
+    w1 = torch.randn(VOCAB, RANK, generator=g, device=dev).to(bf16)
+    w2 = (torch.randn(VOCAB, RANK, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.05).to(bf16)
+    base = torch.randn(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, VOCAB, generator=g, device=dev) * 3
+    s = DSparkSpeculator.__new__(DSparkSpeculator)
+    s.model = _Model(w1, w2, base.to(bf16))
+    s.num_speculative_steps = N_SPEC
+    s._draft_topk = None
+    s.use_confidence_head = False
+    s.acceptance_estimator = None
+    s.draft_watermarker = None
+    s._d2t_scatter_index = None
+    s._draft_scatter_buf = None
+    s.use_fp64_gumbel = False
+    s.draft_logits = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, N_SPEC, VOCAB, dtype=bf16, device=dev)
+    s.temperature = torch.full((MAX_REQS,), temp, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
+    s.seeds = torch.randint(0, 2**62, (MAX_REQS,), generator=g, device=dev)
+    s._step_cols = torch.arange(N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    s.sample_indices = torch.arange(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    # Request slots in another order than the rows, and positions past a
+    # long context, as in the server.
+    slots = torch.tensor([2, 0, 3, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    s.sample_idx_mapping = slots.repeat_interleave(N_SPEC)
+    ctx = torch.tensor([131072, 40000, 7, 99999], dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    steps = torch.arange(N_SPEC, device=dev)
+    s.sample_pos = (ctx[:, None] + 1 + steps[None, :]).flatten()
+    s.input_buffers = SimpleNamespace(
+        input_ids=torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (MAX_REQS * N_SPEC,), generator=g, device=dev)
+    )
+    s._anchor_idx = torch.arange(MAX_REQS, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev) * N_SPEC
+    s.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, N_SPEC, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+    return s
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("temp", [0.0, 0.6, 1.0])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 2])
+def test_fused_markov_matches_vllm_loop(monkeypatch, num_reqs, temp):
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark import fused_markov
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.speculator import DSparkSpeculator
+
+    s = _speculator(temp, seed=int(temp * 10) + num_reqs)
+    hidden = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS * N_SPEC, 8, device="cuda")
+
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=False)
+    DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential(s, num_reqs, hidden)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref_tok, ref_cache = s.draft_tokens.clone(), s.draft_logits.clone()
+
+    s.draft_tokens.zero_()
+    s.draft_logits.zero_()
+    _set_gate(monkeypatch, on=True)
+    try:
+        assert fused_markov.sample_sequential(s, num_reqs, hidden)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    finally:

+
+    slots = s.sample_idx_mapping[: num_reqs * N_SPEC : N_SPEC].long()
+    rc, gc = ref_cache[slots], got_cache[slots]
+    cache_diff = int((rc.view(torch.int16) != gc.view(torch.int16)).sum())
+    tok_diff = int((ref_tok[:num_reqs] != got_tok[:num_reqs]).sum())
+    assert cache_diff <= rc.numel() // 1000, (
+        f"{cache_diff} of {rc.numel()} cached logits differ"
+    )
+    assert tok_diff == 0 or cache_diff > 0, (
+        f"{tok_diff} draft tokens differ while every cached logit is equal"
+    )
